findings.title: getZones reads data.items but backend A4 ListZonesResponse is { zones: [...] } — B2 read/list/map path is fully non-functional at runtime
findings.detail: getZones unwraps a { items } envelope (vehicles/staff CRUD convention) but the real A4 backend returns { zones: [...] }. Runtime trace: getZones -> data.items is undefined -> useZones data undefined -> zonesQuery.data ?? [] -> [] -> ZonesTab list renders empty + ZoneEditorMap zones={[]}. This kills TWO B2 acceptance criteria at runtime: 'ZonesTab lists zones' and 'renders all zones on one labeled map'. It also compounds on create: after createZone success the hook invalidates ['zones'], refetches, gets [] again, so a just-created zone is NEVER visible. This is NOT cosmetic — the entire read/display half of B2 is dead until fixed. Mocked ZonesTab tests hid it (mockGetZones.mockResolvedValue(seedZones) stubs the client fn that does the unwrap, per rules/web-testing.md#network-mocking). CONFIRMED this is the ONLY mis-enveloped client fn added in THIS batch: createZone/updateZone return the bare ZoneDto (no envelope), deleteZone is void, getPriceQuote deserializes the union directly (no envelope). getRoutes/getPlaces are NOT in this batch.
findings.recommendation: DEFERRED to laneB6b per the conductor's pre-made fold-forward decision (laneB6b fixes getZones {items}->{zones} alongside getRoutes/getPlaces). The fold-forward is the right structural call — same envelope-convention set, and tests stay green either way. BLOCK-DECISION CAVEAT: blocks_merge=false is only safe if laneB6a and laneB6b merge to main as a single bundle BEFORE the Zony tab is user-reachable. If laneB6a can land on main independently, there is a window where a FleetAdmin opens a live, permanently-empty, broken Zony tab -> then this SHOULD block and must be fixed in B6a. I did not have the merge-bundling fact in scope; the conductor must confirm bundled merge. Fix when addressed: rename ListZonesResponse.items -> zones, getZones returns data.zones.

findings.title: PriceQuoteView 'unknown' arm + interpretQuote default branch are unreachable
findings.detail: PriceQuoteResponse is an exhaustive discriminated union on type (Fixed|Estimate|Meter) with no other members, so interpretQuote's default -> { kind:'unknown' } and the { kind:'unknown' } view member can never be produced from a well-typed response. Harmless defensive fallback; PriceRangeBadge treats unknown as render-null and RouteOrderPage treats unknown as not-fixed, both correct. Not a correctness issue.
findings.recommendation: Optional: keep as a defensive runtime guard against malformed payloads, or drop the arm + default for a tighter exhaustive switch. No action required.

summary: B1 quote migration is byte-correct against the A6 POST /pricing/quote contract: request body {pickupLat,pickupLng,dropoffLat?,dropoffLng?,at?}; PriceQuoteResponse is a discriminated union on `type` (Fixed{priceCzk,routeId,routeName} | Estimate{lowCzk,highCzk,distanceKm,durationMin} | Meter{baseCzk,perKmCzk,minimumCzk}); interpretQuote switches on `type` (NOT field presence) so A6's emitted null union fields cannot break it, and has a Meter branch (-> kind:'meter', was 'unknown'). PriceRangeBadge.tsx (read + confirmed) renders all three arms: Fixed -> quoteFixed, Meter -> quoteMeter ('Podle taximetru', the new AC#3 behavior), Estimate -> a quoteEstimate RANGE. ALL quote consumers migrated — full-tree grep shows the only getPriceQuote/usePriceQuote/interpretQuote/PriceQuoteResponse consumers are client.ts, priceQuote.ts, usePriceQuote.ts, PriceRangeBadge.tsx, CustomOrderPage(.test).tsx, RouteOrderPage(.test).tsx; NO consumer left on the old {priceType/fromLat/fixedPriceCzk/estimateLowCzk} shape. The .test mock migration is additionally closed by tsc-clean: mockResolvedValue(getPriceQuote) must satisfy the new PriceQuoteResponse union, so an old {priceType,...} mock could not have typechecked. The fromLat/fromLng at board/OrderForm.tsx:290 is useRouteEstimate (a separate geo hook), NOT the pricing/quote client — correctly untouched. Driver priceBadgeUtils/PriceBadge read the ORDER dto priceType/fixedPriceCzk (unchanged by A6) and stay green (AC#6 regression safe). CustomOrderPage.tsx and priceBadgeUtils.ts are unstaged because their contract did not change (CustomOrderPage already used pickupLat arg names; the from->pickup rename was internal to getPriceQuote's call body). RouteOrderPage zone un-stub: Zone/ZoneToZone render pickup (+dropoff) pickers, orderable ONLY on a server Fixed match (kind==='fixed'), out-of-zone -> 'customer.order.outsideZone' with no client-side polygon check; usePriceQuote gained an allowAnonymous opt-in — RouteOrderPage passes true (logged-out in-zone pickup quotes anonymously-by-slug, then reaches inline login), CustomOrderPage leaves it false (stays token-gated, preview-only). B2 zones tab: ZoneEditorMap is React.lazy (its own chunk, not eager in /x initial bundle — ZonesTab references it via lazy() + import type only); pure zoneDraw.ts is Leaflet-free (own haversine) and unit-tested; react-leaflet@4.2.1 reused (no new dep); SettingsPage gains a FleetAdmin-gated (inherited via canAccessSettings) 'Trasy a zony' tab -> RoutesZonesPage with Zony/Trasy/Mista sub-tabs (Trasy/Mista are clean B3/B4 placeholder seams); router.tsx NOT modified; /c and /d untouched; zones CRUD uses hierarchical ['zones'] key with invalidate-on-mutation. ZonesTab.test.tsx (read + confirmed) has the vitest-axe assertion via the preconfigured shared/test/axe helper (AC#4). i18n cs/en parity clean (0 cs-only, 0 en-only; dead zonePlaceholder key removed from both). Touch targets >= theme.touchTargets.min on all new buttons/inputs. No cross-feature imports. No tsconfig.tsbuildinfo / test-results / playwright-report staged. No Windows case collisions. Two findings: F1 getZones {items}->{zones} is a REAL HIGH-severity bug (B2's read/list/map path is non-functional at runtime) already deferred to laneB6b — blocks_merge stays false ONLY under the assumption laneB6a+laneB6b merge as a bundle before the Zony tab is user-reachable; the conductor must confirm that bundling or F1 becomes a blocker in B6a. F2 is an unreachable defensive union arm (LOW/cosmetic).
